findings: The MP client UI context is separate from registered synchronized game/rules scripts. Its namespace function is a no-op and its explicit tick polls commands/production rather than receiving ordinary DroidBuilt events.

wtcmd_finishedUnits is populated only by wtcmd_eventDroidBuilt; the snapshot exposes its last16 entries. The MP private VM does not provide the normal DroidBuilt delivery guarantee, so an empty list is not evidence that native MP production failed.

The MP production tick detects a previously active job whose native factory became idle and retires that active record without appending finishedUnits. Normal native production can therefore complete while that list stays empty.
The short productionFeedback message is deleted after4000ms. A10s observation that misses that message is not a rejected production request.

The shared command report retains the latest100 non-read-only ACK replies in history. Match action queue-production, exact nonce, ok=true, count and factoryId; then independently observe the actual native factory job/progress before opening Players.
state.selectedUnits has only id,x,y,z,order,constructor. It does not expose name. Do not assert a unit name from this field.

The production API uses the native name Design1 display-name plus a stable factory suffix. An actual pre-Players factory production/name observation may be recorded, but it must not be relabelled as a born-unit name read.

For this controlled private fixture, accepted native history+actual factory work before Players, a later new owned combat ID while Players is open, native unit ID/position after normal close, and native selected-ID restoration are meaningful separate observations. Preserve earlier failed helper/name assertions; do not invent missing fields or infer physical paint.
